newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban redouble efforts to hide women.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban redouble efforts to hide women.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban militia has ordered Kabul residents to screen windows in their homes to ensure that women cannot be seen from the street.

The regulations, announced on Taleban-controlled Voice of Sharia radio on Tuesday, told householders to paint any clear glass in their upper windows or replace it with opaque glass up to a height of 180 cm (six feet) from the floor.
The Kabul city council rules mentioned "second-floor windows on both sides of the house, which pose a threat to neighbours as far as Islamic hejab (women's dress code) is concerned".
Householders have until April 9 to comply with the rules or face undisclosed punishment according to Sharia Islamic law.
People planning to build their own houses must follow a plan approved by the city council and construct them "in consideration of the Islamic hejab", the radio said.
A Taleban official in the attorney-general's office in Kabul said on Tuesday that women's faces could corrupt men.
"The face of a woman is a source of corruption for men who are not related to them," said the official, explaining the Taleban edict that women should be veiled in public places.
The Taleban have decreed that women outside their homes must wear the burqa, a shroud-like head-to-toe veil with a small hexagonal patch of gauze over the eyes.
Since capturing Kabul on September 27 the Taleban have enforced their purist version of Islam, banning women from most workplaces and halting most education for girls and women.

The Afghan ambassador at the Taleban-controlled embassy in Islamabad, Mufti Mohammad Masoom Afghani, briefed diplomats and U.N. officials on Tuesday on Taleban "efforts ... to ensure a lasting peace" in Afghanistan, an embassy statement said.
He also told them of Taleban efforts "to combat terrorism and narcotics, collect illegal weapons and ... ensure female education in accordance with the tenets of Islamic Sharia".
